correctness.rationale: Take q=d+r and α=1-ℓq>0. For Φ(y)=||y||^α/(sqrt(2) α) outside radius 2, Itô gives Φ(X_t)=Φ(x)+M_t+∫g(X_s)ds; quadratic-variation density v(y)=(||y||^qπ(y))^-2ℓ→cπ^-2ℓ and radial drift g(y)=||y||^-α (||y||^qπ(y))^-2ℓ[d+α-2+(1-2ℓ)y·∇logπ(y)]/sqrt2→0. Both globally bounded after smooth extension, implying nonexplosion by martingale control. For the upper logarithmic bound, stop or cutoff inside a large ball so v≤v∞+ε; DDS and reflection yield Gaussian exponent -1/[2(v∞+ε)t] per Φ(R)^2. For the lower bound, start in a remote annulus with positive reachability probability in time t-s; choose Brownian paths above -B throughout [0,v_+s] and above H_R throughout [v_-s,v_+s], forcing the radial clock to stay outside radius R0 until s with v_-s≤bracket≤v_+s. The Brownian bridge and Gaussian endpoint exponent give -1/(2v_-s); sending s↑t and ε↓0 matches the upper bound. Because Φ(R)^2=R^(2α)/(2α²), the logarithmic tail coefficient is -cπ^(2ℓ)/(4α² t). Tonelli tail integral establishes strict θ<κt finite, θ>κt infinite; θ=κt remains open. Independently checked transformed algebra exactly on a rational grid and with π=(1+x²)^(-3/2), d=1,r=2,ℓ=.2, radius 10–1000; no finite computation substitutes for the full tail proof.
